newsitem.title: USA: Weather hits US Midwest hog runs, plant operations.
newsitem.headline: Weather hits US Midwest hog runs, plant operations.

text.p: Hog slaughter in the U.S. Midwest Thursday was seen curtailed at several plants in Iowa, South Dakota and Illinois because of wintry weather, company officials and market sources said.

Strong winds in southeastern South Dakota closed country roads and major highways because of poor visibility, limiting hog shipments to the John Morrell and Co. plant in Sioux Falls, according to a plant official.
"There isn't much moving at all because strong winds are blowing snow across roadways and causing white-outs," the plant official said.
John Morrell is a unit of Smithfield Foods Inc.

The official declined to comment on specific plant operations, but said that slaughter would "definitely" be curtailed. The Sioux Falls plant has a daily capacity of about 15,000 head, according to trade estimates.

Travel advisories were posted for southeastern South Dakota due to blizzard conditions and Interstate 90 was closed from Sioux Falls, on the east side of the state, west to Wall, which is about two-thirds of the way across the state near the Black Hills, the state Highway Patrol said.
Interstate 29 in eastern South Dakota was closed "border to border" the Highway Patrol said. Interstate 29 runs north-south.
Some roads in northwest Iowa also were closed because of the weather.
It is too early to tell what impact the weather will have on hog slaughter at IBP Inc's five Iowa plants, said Gary Mickelson, IBP spokesman.
"It most likely will have some impact on slaughter, but we're not sure yet to what degree," Mickelson said.
However, the strong winds had not reached central Iowa.
Light snow was falling in Denison, but not causing any problems, Mickelson said.
Poor road conditions because of heavy snow in west-central and southern Illinois restricted hog supplies to Farmland Industries Inc Farmland Foods plant in Monmouth, Il., a company official said.
"They're a little slow getting in," the official said.
Buying stations in northern Nebraska also were having difficulty securing hogs for Farmland's Crete, Neb. plant because of road conditions, the Farmland official said.
The Monmouth plant has an estimated daily slaughter capacity of 7,000 head and the Crete, Neb. plant has a daily capacity of about 8,300, according to industry projections.
